assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epic Plan table shows two Epics: 'Epic A | TC-9006: trustify-backend | trustify-backend | Tasks 1, 2, 3, 8' and 'Epic B | TC-9006: trustify-ui | trustify-ui | Tasks 4, 5, 6, 7'. The hierarchy is stated as 'Feature -> Epic -> Task hierarchy with by-repository grouping'.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epic Plan table shows Epic A summary as 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and Epic B summary as 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Both match the prescribed format exactly.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Task Summary table shows Epic column: Tasks 1,2,3,8 (trustify-backend) assigned to 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' Epic; Tasks 4,5,6,7 (trustify-ui) assigned to 'TC-9006: trustify-ui' Epic. summary-comment.md confirms: 'Backend (trustify-backend) — Epic A' contains Tasks 1,2,3,8 and 'Frontend (trustify-ui) — Epic B' contains Tasks 4,5,6,7.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md states: 'Incorporates links: Feature TC-9006 links to each Epic (not to individual Tasks).' summary-comment.md elaborates: 'TC-9006 incorporates Epic A (TC-9006: trustify-backend)' and 'TC-9006 incorporates Epic B (TC-9006: trustify-ui)' with explicit note '(Links are from Feature to Epics, not from Feature to individual Tasks.)'

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Task Summary shows: Task 1 (backend, no deps) -> Task 2 (backend, depends Task 1) -> Task 3 (backend, depends Task 2) -> Task 4 (frontend, depends Task 2) -> Task 5 (frontend, depends Task 4) -> Task 6 (frontend, depends Task 5) -> Task 7 (frontend, depends Tasks 5,6) -> Task 8 (backend doc, depends Tasks 1-7). Backend tasks 1,2,3 have lower numbers than dependent frontend tasks 4,5,6,7.

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Non-doc/non-test tasks (1,2,4,5,6) all contain: Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Create, Files to Modify, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Testing tasks (3: 'integration tests', 7: 'tests for remediation dashboard') contain Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements (plus optional sections). Documentation task (8: 'remediation-documentation') contains Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements — no Files to Create/Modify or Implementation Notes, which is acceptable per the exemption.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epic creation details: 'Issue type: Epic (hierarchyLevel 1)' and 'Parent: TC-9006 (the Feature issue)'. summary-comment.md Epics Created table shows 'Issue Type' column as 'Epic (hierarchyLevel 1)' and 'Parent' column as 'TC-9006' for both epics.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 task files have a '## Repository' section with a single value: Tasks 1,2,3,8 have 'trustify-backend'; Tasks 4,5,6,7 have 'trustify-ui'. No task lists multiple repositories.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 task files contain '## Target Branch' (all set to 'main'), '## Description', '## Acceptance Criteria', and '## Test Requirements' sections. Verified in task-1 through task-8.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:', not a placeholder, abbreviated value, or example string
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 digest files exist (task-1-digest.md through task-8-digest.md). Each contains '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-hex>' format. Examples: task-1-digest.md has 'sha256-md:fad761363d3e65131f23e23223f49f93ac2b4c3420ece3e7a524f374526ca0a0', task-2-digest.md has 'sha256-md:da438d2a9117219371f9fc322cb1541c78f77e0ab17c9caa9671e72588ef5db7'. All are 64 lowercase hex characters, not placeholders.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All convention references in Implementation Notes use the prescribed format. Task 1: 'Applies: task creates modules/fundamental/src/remediation/model/summary.rs matching the convention's Rust module file scope.' Task 2: 'Applies: task creates modules/fundamental/src/remediation/endpoints/mod.rs matching the convention's .rs endpoint file scope.' Task 4: 'Applies: task creates src/hooks/useRemediationSummary.ts matching the convention's .ts hook file scope.' Task 5: 'Applies: task creates src/pages/RemediationDashboardPage/RemediationDashboardPage.tsx matching the convention's .tsx page component scope.' No conventions are listed with 'Not applicable' annotations. Backend tasks include only Rust-scoped conventions; frontend tasks include only TypeScript/TSX-scoped conventions — no cross-contamination.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Feature priority is 'Major' (not Undefined). impact-map.md Epic creation details: 'Priority: Major (inherited from Feature)'. summary-comment.md Inherited Field Propagation: 'Priority: Major — propagated to all Epics and Tasks (Feature priority is "Major", which is a valid priority, not "Undefined")'. additional_fields JSON shows '"priority": {"name": "Major"}'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Feature has fixVersions: 'RHTPA 1.5.0' (non-empty). No fixVersion scope config in CLAUDE.md Jira Field Defaults (absent, defaults to 'both'). impact-map.md: 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (inherited from Feature)'. summary-comment.md: 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 — propagated to all Epics and Tasks (Feature has fixVersions set; no fixVersion scope setting found in Jira Field Defaults, so default scope "both" applies)'. additional_fields JSON shows '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in outputs directory and contains '## Inherited Field Propagation' section documenting: 'Priority: Major — propagated to all Epics and Tasks' and 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 — propagated to all Epics and Tasks'. Also includes additional_fields JSON block showing exact values applied to each Epic and Task.
